cases.responsibility: Native iip packet input plus documented callback recorder; white-box state placement and state/RCV.NXT observations
cases.oracle: RFC9293 ordered input model; no-ACK discard, out-of-window RST discard or exact RST reset. Inspect state, RCV.NXT, application callbacks and wire silence; reset drains retransmission buffers.
cases.gaps: Direct state placement; outstanding FIN is actually transmitted where needed. No timestamp negotiation, cryptographic protection or full sequence/window combinations. State placement uses RCV.NXT=10001 after peer FIN at 10000; local FIN is transmitted and, for FIN-WAIT-2/TIME-WAIT, acknowledged. Reachability is covered separately by TCP-TRACE-*.
cases.strength_basis: RFC 9293 3.10.7.4 RST check: exact RCV.NXT reset is an uppercase conditional MUST under RFC 5961, with the same reset required by legacy state processing. Callback and queue checks observe termination.
cases.oracle_review: Direct state/sequence placement; independently specified state/flag rules with wire, delivery and internal state checks. Placement does not establish reachability; mode-specific ACK/state rows share a helper.

cases.applicability: IPv4; placed synchronized state; no timestamps; RFC9293 reset processing
cases.responsibility: iip with packet backend and documented application callbacks; no substitute TCP
cases.oracle: Independent RFC input model: state, RCV.NXT/SND.UNA, application byte/FIN/close callbacks; required wire replies and checksums. Outstanding local FIN is actually transmitted.

cases.applicability: IPv4; placed synchronized state; no timestamps; RFC9293 reset processing
cases.responsibility: iip with packet backend and documented application callbacks; no substitute TCP

cases.strength_basis: End-to-end trace of RFC 9293 3.10.7.3/3.10.7.4 state-processing and 3.10.8 retransmission rules, not a single uppercase MUST. Protocol violations remain FAIL.
cases.oracle_review: Wire-driven connection transitions plus internal state/sequence assertions; independent transition trace does not imply an opaque-state oracle.

cases.description: Exact TCP frame truncated to 0 bytes with original IPv4 length
cases.applicability: IPv4 over Ethernet; native input path; exact-size receive allocation; fabricated TCP fixture
cases.responsibility: iip + packet backend and payload observation callbacks; no input-filter substitute
cases.oracle: No application delivery from malformed input, no sanitizer error, then valid TCP bytes and UDP length/first byte in the same workspace. Each case isolated; diagnostics identify physical length and recovery outcomes. Recovery is compared with a fresh same-state clean TCP/UDP control. A matching recovery with a failing clean control is INCONCLUSIVE and names MAL-VALID-*; malformed delivery/state/silence violations and differential recovery remain FAIL.
cases.gaps: Finite input set; ASan/UBSan success is not a proof of memory safety. No leak assertion. See README.md#malformed-input-and-recovery for reset policy, maximum lengths and callback limits.
cases.requirement: TCP base header, Data Offset, options and checksum must describe an available segment. Illegal option lengths must be handled gracefully (MUST-7); reset is recommended, not required. Exact-buffer safety and recovery are robustness properties.
cases.oracle_review: Byte-built malformed input; placed TCP state and same-state clean control compare wire, callbacks and internal state. UDP callbacks observe length/first byte, not a complete application stream. No option-error adapter enabled.

cases.description: Reject reversed/empty SACK blocks with valid-block and retransmission controls
cases.applicability: Placed ESTABLISHED IPv4 fixture; SACK enabled; 24-byte flight at sequence 4096.
cases.requirement: SACK left edge denotes first byte received and right edge the byte immediately following the block. Selected robustness profile: reversed/empty blocks cannot add scoreboard entries or free unacknowledged bytes.
cases.oracle: Inspect scoreboard and retained buffers after reversed/empty blocks; valid block positive control; wire retransmission of first hole with known bytes/checksum.
cases.oracle_review: Placed sender state and internal scoreboard/buffer checks; wire recovery supplement. Does not require a particular congestion recovery algorithm.

cases.description: Native FIN reports EOF exactly once, including duplicate FIN
cases.applicability: Native active IPv4 handshake; peer sends three bytes then FIN; no Linux dependency.
cases.requirement: Receive processing signals the user when the peer closes its sending direction. Callback ABI maps this notification to CLOSE_WAIT; duplicate FIN must not duplicate that notification.
cases.oracle: Independent peer sequence and wire ACK; exact application bytes, EOF=0 before FIN and EOF=1 after FIN and duplicate FIN; native reset CLOSED control.
cases.oracle_review: Native OPEN/RUN and byte-built peer; no target connection state, queues or sequence helpers for expected results. Uses shared documented callback ABI.

oracle_dependencies.packet-clock-abi: Test-owned packet allocation, link/IP identity and virtual clock. Native callbacks are bound through test_backend.c; payload slices use the iip descriptor ABI. This is the evaluated integration, not standalone iip.
oracle_dependencies.legacy-fixture: Scenario can place connection/sequence/timer state, call internal helpers, or inspect internal fields. External output assertions do not remove those preconditions.
oracle_dependencies.derived-events: test_api_record_run_events derives transitions/retransmission/loss from internal before/after snapshots. CLOSED reason reads CLOSE_RST in iip_ops_tcp_closed; these are not independent native event interfaces.
oracle_dependencies.isn-hook: IIP_OPS_TCP_CONN_INIT adds the test-owned BLAKE2 tuple offset and updates sequence fields. Keyed PRF implementation/serialization is supplied by the harness.
oracle_dependencies.listen-table: test_tcp_listen and iip_ops_tcp_accept implement listener matching/table policy in the test backend; native iip processes accepted TCP handshakes.
oracle_dependencies.source-selector: test_tcp_active_open/test_ip4_select_source_address implement optional local-address selection and queries in the harness.
oracle_dependencies.source-route: test_capture_return_route/test_backend_ipv4_opt_send implement route capture, reversal and precedence. Wire output measures integration, not native routing policy.
oracle_dependencies.input-filter: test_backend_ipv4_tcp_input_filter discards broadcast/multicast traffic before native TCP processing. Discard policy is supplied by this callback.
oracle_dependencies.ip4-option-error: test_backend_ip4_option_error validates malformed options and crafts ICMP Parameter Problem before iip_run. PASS does not establish native option validation.
oracle_dependencies.udp-port-error: test_backend_udp implements port binding and crafts ICMP Port Unreachable. PASS does not establish a native UDP socket table.
oracle_dependencies.tfo-cookie: test_tcp_fastopen_request/check generate and validate cookies with test-owned BLAKE2/key policy. iip transport treatment of callback results remains under test.
oracle_dependencies.capacity-fault: packet_capacity_sequence and clone tracking substitute allocator capacity/failure conditions; these do not implement TCP behavior.
oracle_dependencies.scripted-wire-peer: Raw byte peer with independent sequence arithmetic, checksum and bounded parser. No native connection-state reads; pool/clock initialization remains test supplied.
oracle_dependencies.linux-reference: A separate Linux AF_INET/SOCK_STREAM loopback executes the same application writes/half-close trace. Compare explicit expected bytes/EOF as well as each other; not direct interoperability or RFC proof.
oracle_dependencies.harness-self: Self-tests include synthetic events, packet builders and two iip endpoints. Synthetic callback/event tests are harness validation, not target conformance.
oracle_dependencies.configuration-fields: Nagle/keepalive/retransmission-limit/Diffserv configuration helpers write connection fields directly. They supply the control binding; transport effects remain native. This does not validate a native setter API.
